note: Discovery leads for hands-on Python topic workers. Every topic must independently read and verify its sources. Correct, idiomatic, version-current executable examples are the defining control: execute every code sample with python3 before publication.

tierA.useFor: authoritative Python 3 language, library, tutorial, packaging, testing, exceptions, and data-model semantics
authoritative rationale and specifications where a language feature needs historical or design context
authoritative packaging, virtual-environment, distribution, and dependency guidance

tierB.useFor: open textbook explanations and small introductory examples; synthesize in original prose
supplementary visual traces only; verify all semantic claims against official documentation
supplementary testing examples; distinguish third-party pytest from Python's standard unittest module

cautions: CORRECTNESS IS THE PRIMARY CONTROL. Execute every Python code block, expression, output claim, numeric trace, and algorithmic assertion with python3 before publishing. Use idiomatic, version-current Python 3; do not rely on Python 2 behavior or undocumented implementation details.

Use the official Python documentation as the primary authority for language and standard-library behavior. Reuse an existing source-registry id exactly when it has the same URL; do not mint parallel ids for the same Python documentation page.

Teach language semantics precisely: indentation forms suites; equality (==) differs from identity (is); mutable objects and aliases can share state; dict and set order behavior must be stated only as documented; a Python list is a mutable dynamic array, not a linked list. Separate built-ins, standard library modules, third-party packages, and user code.

Keep adjacent lessons distinct: Installing Python owns interpreter acquisition and version checks; Running Python Programs owns REPL versus script execution; Python Syntax owns lexical/indentation conventions; Variables owns names and binding; Numbers owns arithmetic; Strings owns text sequences; Booleans owns truth values; Type Conversion owns explicit conversions. Do not turn one topic into a survey of the whole subject.

For files, use safe and portable examples: context managers (with open(...)) and explicit encodings when text encoding matters; keep Reading Files, Writing Files, and Files distinct. For exceptions, teach targeted handling and avoid bare except. For packages, distinguish import packages from installable distributions and cite PyPA guidance.

For introductory data analysis, keep claims modest and reproducible: show small, standard-library examples unless an external library is specifically introduced and sourced. Do not imply that a small example establishes a real-world conclusion.

The final queue entry is a mis-ingested instruction header. Keep its slug but retitle it as a genuine lesson about building and verifying small executable Python examples; do not write a meta instruction as a lesson.

Distribute question answer keys EVENLY across A/B/C/D, ensuring at least one C and one D per topic. Verify keys yourself from the file, and avoid reusing identical question-stem templates across topics.
